- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.5) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply +1.5–2.5% bias to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- When sentiment swings from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model lags; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward correction of 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For sentiment history with alternating highs/lows, model tends to overfit recent sentiment; use 2–3 day moving average of sentiment to smooth forecast bias.
